reason: The passage depicts multiple human characters demonstrating agency throughout the narrative. The people of Israel collectively gather and address David directly about his leadership (וַיִּקָּבְצוּ כָל־ יִשְׂרָאֵל), the elders of Israel come before the king and make a covenant with him (וַ֠יָּבֹאוּ כָּל־ זִקְנֵ֨י יִשְׂרָאֵ֤ל), and they actively anoint him as king. Additionally, the passage catalogs numerous military figures like Jashobeam, Eleazar, Benaiah and others, each performing specific deeds and actions that define their character. Even David himself makes declarations and choices (e.g., his statement about who strikes the Jebusites first). While some are exceptional warriors (gibborim), they remain human agents who make decisions and take actions that drive the narrative forward.
